question: What is the IRS limit on employee elective deferrals to a 401(k) plan for 2027?
answer:
The IRS limit on employee elective deferrals to a 401(k) plan for 2027 is $25,500, up from $24,500 for 2026, as announced on November 12, 2026 [2]. The same limit applies to 403(b) plans, governmental 457 plans and the Thrift Savings Plan [2]. Notice 2026-66 confirms the increase under section 402(g)(1) [1].

Eligible participants aged 50 and over can make catch-up contributions in addition to the basic limit [2]. For most of these plans, the catch-up limit for people aged 50 and over rises to $8,500, so they can generally contribute up to $34,000 in 2027 [2]. Those aged 60 through 63 have a higher catch-up limit of $11,750 [2].

This is general information, not personalized advice. Decisions about your own contributions are worth discussing with a qualified professional.

keyPoints.text: The 2027 limit on employee elective deferrals to a 401(k) plan is $25,500, up from $24,500 for 2026.
The $25,500 limit also applies to 403(b), governmental 457 plans, and the federal Thrift Savings Plan.
Employees aged 50 and over can contribute up to $34,000 in 2027 with the standard catch-up of $8,500.
The 2027 figures come from IRS Notice 2026-66 and an IRS news release dated November 12, 2026.

mayBeStale.text: The 2026 draft Publication 525 shows the 2026 401(k) limit of $24,500 and is superseded for 2027 purposes.
